# Upgrade Fixtures

These fixtures are generated by the tagged KoutenDB releases named below, not
by the current source tree. They preserve the internal files needed to exercise
real pre-v1 upgrade boundaries.

| Fixture | Source commit | Physical layout |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.10.1` | `7ef997b2029179aa3ac32cdf88df73a07bb32f13` | Versioned WAL plus a legacy generation-zero segment without a manifest or sidecar index |
| `v0.11.0` | `40c5e43cdf31baff6b3ffcc763003bb5456996af` | Versioned WAL plus manifest-selected generation-one segments and indexes |

Each fixture contains JSON, raw, NIF, and BIF payloads, vectors, an update, a
delete, an embedded transaction, ring metadata, and enough records to create a
physical segment. `original-dump.jsonl` is the logical reference exported by
the same tagged release.

The tests always copy these directories before opening them. The committed
fixtures are immutable test inputs and must never be opened in place.

## Regeneration

`generate_fixture.nim` is the common generator used for both releases. Extract
the target tag, copy the generator into the same relative path, and compile it
against that tag's `src/` directory:

```sh
nim c --path:src -d:release tests/fixtures/generate_fixture.nim
```

For v0.11.0, also pass `-d:koutenManifestFixture` so the generator explicitly
packs each populated ring into a manifest-selected generation. Run the binary
with a fresh data directory and dump path. Only `kouten.log`, `segments/`, and
the JSONL dump belong in a committed fixture; lock and audit files are runtime
artifacts. Confirm the source tag and commit in `fixture.json` before replacing
an existing fixture.
